subject: ba
title: Nature of Business
objectives: Define business and identify what separates it from other human activity.
Contrast the traditional and modern concepts of business.
study:
Business describes organised, repeated activity aimed at producing, exchanging, or distributing goods and services — not a one-off transaction, and not activity carried out purely for personal consumption. What separates business from other human effort is the intent behind it: it is undertaken to earn some kind of return, whether that return is profit, prestige, or simple satisfaction.

Key termBusiness — organised economic activity, repeated over time, directed at producing, exchanging or distributing goods and services in pursuit of a return.

Two ways of framing why business exists sit alongside each other in the literature. The traditional view treats profit as the whole point: a business exists to maximise returns for its owners. The modern view widens the lens — profit still matters, but it's earned while satisfying customers and acting as a responsible part of the wider society the business operates in.

Exam tipQuestions often ask you to contrast these two concepts directly — know the shift in emphasis from "profit alone" to "profit plus social responsibility."

Human activity more broadly splits into economic activity (anything tied to producing wealth — further divided into profession, employment, and business) and non-economic activity (voluntary or social effort with no profit motive attached). Business is one branch of the economic side, distinguished from profession and employment by the specific pattern of buying, producing and selling for a return.
recap:
• Business = repeated, organised activity to produce/exchange/distribute goods or services for a return.
  • Traditional concept: profit maximisation is the goal.
  • Modern concept: consumer satisfaction plus social responsibility, profit as one outcome among several.
  • Economic activity (profession, employment, business) vs non-economic activity (no profit motive).
